entries.sanskrit:
षष्ठे सख्युर् गिरा नन्दो व्रजं गच्छन् मृतां पथि ।

दृष्ट्वा तु राक्षसीं तस्या मृत्युं श्रुत्वाथ विस्मितः ॥१॥
entries.literal_english: In the sixth chapter, while going to Vraja on the word of his friend, Nanda saw the dead Rākṣasī on the road and, after hearing of her death, became astonished.

entries.sanskrit: कृष्ण-विषये शङ्कमानं राजानं प्रत्य् अविषये प्रवृत्ता सैव मरिष्यतीति सूचयन्न् आह---न यत्रेति । यत्र श्री-कृष्णस्य श्रवणादीनि न सन्ति, तत्रैव तासां शक्तिः, साक्षात् तस्मिन्न् एव सति का शङ्केति भावः ॥३॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara says that the power of the Rākṣasī is present where hearing and the other devotional acts concerning Śrī Kṛṣṇa are absent; when He Himself is present, what fear could there be? The verse therefore warns Kaṁsa that she will die in a place where those acts are absent.

entries.sanskrit: चराचरात्मत्वाद् एव तां विबुध्य निमीलितेक्षण आस । स्वयम् अनन्तं दुष्टानाम् अन्तकं बालं मत्वा सा अङ्कम् आरोपयत् । यथोरगं सुप्तम् अबुद्धिश् चासौ रज्जु-धीश् च सोऽज्ञानतो रज्जु-बुद्ध्या गृह्णाति तद्वत् ॥८
word_for_word: because she is the self of moving and unmoving
entries.literal_english: Knowing that she was the self of all moving and unmoving beings, she closed her eyes. Thinking the child Himself to be the endless end of the wicked, she placed Him on her lap. Her ignorance is like that of someone who sees a sleeping snake, mistakes a rope for a rope, and grasps it under that false understanding.

entries.sanskrit: ननु यशोदा-रोहिण्यौ तां कथं न न्यवारयेतां ? तत्राह---ताम् इति । वामं वल्गु जनन्या इव चेष्टितं यस्यास् तां वर-स्त्रियं च सहसैवान्तरा गृह-मध्ये वीक्ष्य । अन्तस् तैक्ष्ण्ये बहिर् मार्दवे च दृष्टान्तः---कोश-परिच्छदासिवत् । मृदु-चित्र-चर्म-मयः कोशः परिच्छद आवरणं यस्यासेः खड्गस्य, तद्वत् । तत्-प्रभयाच धर्षितेऽभिभूते । "अहम् अस्य जननी इयं वा ?" इति मोहिते च सत्यौ जननी जनन्यौ निरीक्षमाणे एव केवलम् अतिष्ठतां, न तु निवारितवत्यौ ॥९॥
entries.literal_english: Why did Yaśodā and Rohiṇī not restrain her? They saw the beautiful woman suddenly appear within the house, moving with the shameless boldness of a mother. Her inner sharpness and outer softness are compared to a sword in its sheath: the sheath is made of soft, painted leather and covers the sword. Overwhelmed by her radiance and bewildered—‘Am I this child’s mother, or is she?’—the two mothers merely stood watching and did not restrain her.

entries.sanskrit: व्यादाय मुखं विवृत्य । निज-रूपम् आस्थिता मरण-समये कपटम् अयुक्तम् इतीव ॥
entries.literal_english: She opened her mouth wide. At the moment of death she assumed her own real form, as though deception had become inappropriate.

entries.literal_english: Even while falling, her body crushed the trees that stood within the surrounding cloth-like enclosure.

entries.sanskrit:
ईषा-मात्रोग्र-दंष्ट्रास्यम्, ईषा लाङ्गल-दण्डस् तत् प्रमाणोग्रा दंष्ट्रा यस्मिंस् तत् तथा-भूतम् आस्यं यस्मिंस् तत् तस्याः कलेवरं वीक्ष्य गोपा गोप्यश् च सन्त-त्रसुः । सन्त्रास-हेतुत्वेन पुनर् अष्टभिः पदैर् विशिनष्टि । गिरि-कन्दर-वन्-नासिके यस्मिंस् तत् । गिरेश् च्युतौ स्थूलोपलौ ताव् इव स्तनौ यस्मिंस् तत् । रौद्रं घोरम् । प्रकीर्णा अरुणा मूर्ध-जा यस्मिंस् तत् ॥

अन्ध-कूपाव् इव गभीरे अक्षिणी यस्मिंस् तत् । पुलिन-वद् आरोहौ जघने ताभ्यां भीषणम् । बद्धाः सेतव इव भूजौ ऊरू अङ्घ्री च यस्मिंस् तत् । शून्य-तोय-ह्रद इवोदरं यस्मिंस् तत् ॥

पूर्वम् एव तस्याः शब्देन भीताः पुनर्-दर्शनेनातित-त्रसुर् इत्य् आह---पूर्वं त्व् इति । तस्याः निःस्वनितं शब्दस् तेन निर्भिन्नानि हृत्-कर्ण-मस्तकानि येषां ते ॥
entries.literal_english: The cowherds and cowherd women saw a body whose mouth had terrible fangs as large as a plough-pole, and they were terrified. Śrīdhara then specifies the frightening features: a nose like a mountain cave; breasts like huge rocks fallen from a mountain; a dreadful body; scattered red hair; eyes as deep as abandoned wells; hips like sandbanks, making them terrifying; arms and thighs and feet like bound bridges; and a belly like a waterless lake. They had already been frightened by her roar; seeing her again terrified them even more, for the sound had split their hearts, ears and heads.

entries.sanskrit: अनाचान्ता एव प्रथममति-सम्भ्रमेणैव रक्षां कृत्वा किञ्चिल् लब्धश् चासाः पुनस् तात्पर्येण बीज-न्यासम् अकुर्वतेत्य् आह---गोप्य इति । संस्पृष्ट-सलिला आचान्ताः आत्मनि प्रथमम् अङ्गेषु करयोश् च पृथक् । अजाद्य्-एकादश-बीजानां मध्ये कर-शुद्धौ त्रीणि, करयोः सन्धिषु चत्वारि चत्वारि, तथा अङ्घ्र्य्-आदाव् एकैकस्मिन्न् अङ्गे अजाद्य्-एकैकं बोजं न्यस्य बालस्याप्य् अङ्गेषु तथैवाकुर्वत् ॥
entries.literal_english: At first the Gopīs had not performed ācamana, being confused by the sudden danger; after obtaining a little water they made a protective rite. Then, having touched water and performed ācamana, they placed the seed-syllables with intention. They performed the rite first on themselves, separately on the limbs and hands: of the eleven seed-syllables, three were used for purification of the hands, four at each of the joints of the hands, and one each on the feet and on each limb beginning with the head. They performed the same rite on the child’s limbs.

entries.sanskrit: तथा दिक्षु रक्षाम् अकुर्वन्न् इत्य् आह---चक्र्य् अग्रत इति । चक्र-सहितो हरिस् तवाग्रतोऽस्तु । सह-गदो गदासहितो हरिस् तव पश्चाद् अस्तु । त्वत्-पार्श्वयोर् धनुर्-धरो मधु-हासि-धरोऽजनश् चैताव् आस्ताम् । शङ्ख-घर उरुगायश् चतुष्-कोणेषु । क्षिताव् अधस् तात् ॥
word_for_word: bearer of the weapon that killed Madhu
entries.literal_english: They also made protection in the directions. ‘May Hari with His discus be before you; may Hari with His mace be behind you. May the bow-bearer and the bearer of the weapon that killed Madhu stand at your sides. May the conch-bearing, widely praised Lord stand in the four directions; may He protect you below, on the earth.’

entries.literal_english: Having made external protection in this way, they made the internal protection, as is indicated by the word ‘senses.’

entries.sanskrit: विस्मयम् एवाह---नूनम् इति । बत विस्मये । सांप्रतं स ऋषिस् तपः-प्रभाववान् योगेशो ज्ञानी वा सम्यग् आस । यतः स एव दृष्ट इति ॥
entries.literal_english: This is an expression of astonishment. ‘Surely that ṛṣi was then fully accomplished through the power of austerity, or was a lord of yoga, or was a knower, since he alone was seen.’

entries.sanskrit: विस्मयान्तरम् आह---दह्यमानस्येति । कृष्णेन निर्भुक्तोऽत एव सपद्य् आहतः पाप्मा यस्य ॥३४॥
entries.literal_english: Another astonishment is stated: while being burned, her sin had been consumed by Kṛṣṇa; therefore the sinful force that belonged to her was struck down immediately.

entries.sanskrit: प्रसङ्गात् कैमुत्य-न्यायेन भक्ति-वैभवम् आह---पूतनेति ॥ श्रद्धया आस्तिक्येन भक्त्या प्रेम्णा । रक्ताः स्निग्धाः । तन्-मातर इति वत्साहरण-लीलाभिप्रायेण बहु-वचनम् । गो-गोपिकास् तदा मातरोऽभवन्न् इति ॥३५-३६॥
word_for_word: by the logic of a stronger case
entries.literal_english: Taking the occasion, Śrīdhara explains the greatness of devotion by the logic of an even stronger case. Through faith, conviction, devotion and love, the cowherd women were attached to Kṛṣṇa. They were called ‘their mothers’ in the plural with reference to the later pastime in which the calves were stolen and the cows and cowherd women became their mothers.
